key_insight: Sparse AFM scans are expanded into a probabilistic ensemble of plant cell-wall microstructures, enabling distributions of effective elastic properties and macroscale tensile response instead of a single constitutive estimate.
engineering_relevance: This provides a scalable way to translate limited nanoscale observations into uncertainty-aware continuum mechanics models for fibrous biological materials.
method: Fine-tune Stable Diffusion with LoRA on AFM images to generate AFM-like wall microstructure ensembles.
Convert each synthetic microstructure into spatially varying Young’s modulus and Poisson’s ratio fields, then run strain-controlled finite-element homogenization.
Sweep matrix-to-fibril stiffness ratios and propagate the resulting effective-property distributions into stochastic tensile simulations of a larger specimen.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluation of synthetic images using microfibril crossover count and crossover angle, plus stochastic homogenization results that produce distributions—and sometimes multimodal behavior—of effective moduli and stress response.
watch_item: Quantitative prediction still depends on calibrating the intensity-to-property mapping against nanomechanical measurements, so the current workflow is not yet fully predictive at the fiber scale.
paper_title: From Sparse AFM Observations to Probabilistic Macroscale Mechanics: A Generative-Physics Framework for Plant Cell Walls
